svg.title: Corvin A2A — a large object travels as a signed reference and is pulled over a signed op (ADR-2287)
svg.desc: Sequence between a requester and the holder (the peer whose worker wrote the file). Files up to 1 MiB in total travel inline in the signed response. A larger file passes the object gate (name, size ceiling, L34 classification, L35 egress), is audited as issued and becomes a reference with no content inside the signed response. The requester pulls it chunk by chunk with signed object-pull requests riding on the ping transport, direct or over the relay. The holder checks the signatures, the origin binding, the TTL, the replay ledger, the pull budget and the same gate again, audits each chunk before serving it, and signs every answer. The requester accepts the object only if the final sha256 equals the signed reference.
svg.text: Large objects: a signed reference, then a signed pull
Inline stays for up to 1 MiB in total (16 files). Above that the bytes stay with the holder until the requester asks.
Requester (sender)
Holder (peer, its worker)
direct HTTP, or the relay when the direct route is dead
1 signed TaskEnvelope — result_schema asks attachments_by_reference
2 worker writes out/film.bin (12 MiB)
over the inline budget: copied to the object store staging area
object gate: name · size ceiling (origin, operator) · L34 class
vs the origin's max · L35 egress to the origin's host
audit first: A2A.object_issued (prefixes, size, class, origin)
3 signed response: small files inline, the large one as a reference
{name, mime, size, sha256, classification, ref_id, inline: false}
loop per chunk (≤ 1 MiB)
4 signed ping + object_pull {ref_id, offset, length} + pull_sig (fresh ping id)
ping + pull signatures · freshness · pull rate bucket
origin-bound · TTL (15 min, ≤ 24 h) · replay ledger
budget (max_pulls × size) · the same object gate again
audit first: A2A.object_pulled, then the chunk
5 signed pong + object_chunk {ref_id, offset, length, data_b64} — or object_refusal
6 final sha256 == signed sha256
only then the object lands (file renamed into place);
otherwise object_digest_mismatch and nothing is kept
Closed refusals (never a hint, never a byte)
unknown = expired = another origin's → object_unavailable
object_pull_replayed · object_pull_budget_exhausted · object_bad_range
object_classification_exceeded · object_egress_denied · object_too_large
old holder (plain pong) → object_pull_unsupported
bad pull signature → the opaque 403 of a bad ping
Store: <tenant>/global/a2a_feed/objects/ — outside the worker's cwd,
erased with the peer (L36, L-a2a-feed), swept at TTL.
